title: Check if Binary String Has at Most One Segment of Ones
statement: `s` is a string of `'0'` and `'1'` characters whose first character is `'1'`. A segment of ones is a maximal run of consecutive `'1'` characters. Return `true` when `s` has no more than one such segment, and `false` when it has two or more.
notes:
## Intuition

Because `s` starts with `'1'`, the first segment of ones always begins at index 0. A second segment can only start at a `'1'` that comes after some `'0'`. So scan left to right, remember whether a zero has appeared, and fail as soon as a one shows up after it. (A slower but obvious check splits `s` on `'0'` and counts the non-empty pieces.)

## Approach

1. Set `seenZero = false`.
2. For each character `ch` of `s`:
   - if `ch` is `'0'`, set `seenZero = true`;
   - otherwise, if `seenZero` is already true, this one starts a new segment, so return `false`.
3. If the loop ends, all ones were in the leading run; return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "1001"`.

- `'1'`: no zero yet, keep going.
- `'0'`: `seenZero = true`.
- `'0'`: still true.
- `'1'`: a one after a zero, so a second segment starts; return `false`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the string.
- Space: O(1): a single flag.

## Pitfalls

- A string of only ones (`"111"`) or ones followed only by zeros (`"1100"`) is `true`; trailing zeros do not create a segment.
- Do not count zero runs: `"1001"` and `"10"` both have one zero run but different answers.
- The flag must never reset to false when a one appears, or `"10101"` would pass.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seenZero` | whether any `'0'` has appeared so far |
| `ch` | the current character |

narration.2: No zero has appeared yet; we are still inside the leading run of ones.
narration.3: Look at each character from left to right.
narration.4: A zero ends the leading run of ones.
narration.5: Remember that the first segment is over.
narration.6: A one after a zero would start a second segment.
narration.7: Two segments exist, so the answer is false.
narration.10: No one ever followed a zero, so there is at most one segment.
